headline: Recent lockdowns expected to crimp earnings for retailers and mobility-dependent companies in FY21 and potentially FY22
reasoning: Fairview notes that recent lockdowns will affect retailers and mobility-dependent industries such as travel, potentially crimping both FY21 and FY22 earnings upside. Management teams are expected to be cautious about providing definitive guidance, with most likely waiting until their AGMs. Areas of concern heading into reporting season include margins, pricing power, labour availability, supply chain issues and the ability to sustain pandemic-induced sales levels.
quote: But without question recent lockdowns will crimp some companies FY21, and possibly FY22, upside earnings riskpotential. Retailers and mobility-dependent industries such as travel will be affected. Additionally, it is expected to curb the confidence of boards and management teams to provide definitive outlook statements and guidance (most will wait until at least their AGMs). Other areas of interest will be margins, pricing power, labour availability, supply chain issues as well as how the market treats companies who struggle to match their lofty pandemic-induced sales levels.

headline: Bumper domestic consumer spending driving earnings upgrades across consumer-facing small caps as household savings fall and international travel spending redirected domestically
reasoning: Fairview notes that over a third of the 30+ small cap companies receiving meaningful analyst earnings upgrades (>2%) during May 2021 were consumer-facing. The household savings rate continues to fall from its 2020 highs, the federal budget was more stimulatory than expected, and the A$65bn not being spent on international travel is washing through the domestic economy. The Melbourne lockdown has also accelerated vaccination take-up, supporting prospects for a less interrupted recovery and potential border re-opening.
quote: Bumper domestic consumer spending continues. There are few positives from the Melbourne lockdown, but clearly the vaccination take-up rate has accelerated which will support the prospect of a less interrupted economic recovery as well as the chance for international borders to re-open. In the meantime, the household saving rate continues to fall from its lofty high of 22% in mid-2020, the Federal Government's May budget was more stimulatory than expected, and the A$65bn not being spent on international travel continues to wash through the domestic economy. All this is aiding retailers as they cycle the excessive growth rates experienced last year. In fact, of the 30+ small cap companies to see meaningful (+2%) analyst earnings upgrades during May, over a third were consumer-facing.

headline: Fairview aligns with Janet Yellen's view that inflation may have escaped the bottle, citing widespread company commentary on rising input costs, supply chain constraints, and higher commodity and freight prices
reasoning: US Q1 earnings were strong overall, with 87% of S&P 500 reporters beating consensus expectations by an average of 23%. However, key themes were inflationary: supply chain constraints (particularly semiconductor shortages), higher raw material costs, rising freight costs due to shipping container shortages, and staff unavailability in some sectors. The same themes were evident in Australian company communications at recent broker conferences. Fairview notes they have not heard a single company mention stable input costs or flat pricing, aligning with the view that inflation may be structurally rising.
quote: While not professing to be economists, we're in the Janet Yellen camp, who mentioned the inflation genie may have escaped the bottle, as we're yet to hear a company mention stable input costs or that their pricing isn't going higher. Key takeaways have been the continued reopening momentum as well as inflationary pressures. Management teams are focused on supply chain constraints (especially the semiconductor demand/supply imbalance), higher raw materials (commodity prices) and freight costs, due to a lingering shipping container shortage.
